title: What order comes out of the tree?
hook: Seven keys go into a search tree in a jumbled order. Walk it one way. What comes out?

knows: a binary search tree is built by inserting keys, smaller left, bigger right (lopsided-tree)
doesNotKnow: that reading left side, node, right side (in-order) gives the keys in sorted order

misconception: Reading a search tree gives the keys in the order they were inserted.
objective: The learner can walk the tree built from 5, 3, 8, 1, 4, 9, 7 left-node-right, get 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, and explain why that order is always sorted.

claims.text: Inserting 5, 3, 8, 1, 4, 9, 7 (smaller left, bigger right) gives a tree with 5 at the top, 3 and 8 below it, and 1, 4, 7, 9 at the bottom.
claims.source: Demo.tsx build(); builder traced the inserts by hand: 3<5 left, 8>5 right, 1<3 left, 4 in (3,5) right of 3, 9>8 right, 7 in (5,8) left of 8.

claims.text: Reading left side, then the node, then the right side visits 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9.
claims.source: Demo.tsx inorder(ROOT) = [1,3,4,5,7,8,9]. Option B, node-first (pre-order), is 5, 3, 1, 4, 8, 7, 9 (preorder(ROOT)).

claims.text: Every key on a node's left is smaller and every key on its right is bigger, so the left-node-right walk of a search tree is always sorted.
claims.source: CLRS (3rd ed.) 12.1: the binary-search-tree property lets INORDER-TREE-WALK print keys in sorted order; proof by induction on subtrees.
Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 1, 2.3.1 (symmetric order, also called inorder); CLRS 12.1 'inorder tree walk'.

recall.question: Keys 6, 2, 9, 4 go into a search tree. What does the left-side, node, right-side walk list?
recall.why: The in-order walk of any search tree lists the keys smallest to largest, whatever order they went in.
